C1.label: unsupported
C1.reason: evidence bears on the claim but no supporting argument was built
C1.text: Initiating low-dose aspirin produces a net reduction in cardiovascular harm in adults aged 60 and older, with cardiovascular benefits outweighing bleeding harms and any mortality effects.

C2.label: defeated
C2.reason: all constructed support is out, withdrawn or inapplicable
C2.text: Initiating low-dose aspirin produces a net increase in harm in adults aged 60 and older, with bleeding harms and any adverse mortality effects outweighing cardiovascular benefits.

C5.label: accepted
C5.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C5.text: Primary-prevention trials include community-dwelling adults aged 70 and older without established cardiovascular disease, providing direct evidence for older adults.

C7.label: accepted
C7.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C7.text: Primary-prevention trials involving adults aged 60 and older compare low-dose aspirin with placebo over multiple years and report cardiovascular events, mortality, and bleeding outcomes.

C8.label: refuted
C8.text: No primary-prevention trials or reported age subgroups have studied low-dose aspirin in adults aged 60 and older.

C10.label: unsupported
C10.reason: evidence bears on the claim but no supporting argument was built
C10.text: Initiating low-dose aspirin leaves cardiovascular and all-cause mortality materially unchanged in adults aged 60 and older without established cardiovascular disease.

C12.label: unsupported
C12.reason: evidence bears on the claim but no supporting argument was built
C12.text: Initiating low-dose aspirin has no effect on cardiovascular events or mortality in adults aged 60 and older without established cardiovascular disease.

C16.label: refuted
C16.text: Initiating low-dose aspirin does not increase major bleeding or other clinically important treatment-related harms in adults aged 60 and older.

C18.label: accepted
C18.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C18.text: USPSTF modeling reports slightly negative to slightly positive lifetime quality-adjusted gains for initiation in the sixties, but losses in quality-adjusted and unadjusted life-years in the seventies across nearly all modeled risks.

C19.label: accepted
C19.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C19.text: The cited review describes ARRIVE as enrolling adults aged at least fifty-five at moderate cardiovascular risk without diabetes, and ASCEND as enrolling adults aged at least forty with diabetes.

C20.label: accepted
C20.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C20.text: Mixed-age low-dose aspirin trial pools reported modest reductions in nonfatal myocardial infarction and nonfatal ischemic stroke.

C21.label: accepted
C21.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C21.text: ASPREE reported higher all-cause mortality with aspirin than placebo over median follow-up of 4.7 years.

C22.label: accepted
C22.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C22.text: In ASPREE's healthy older population, aspirin increased major hemorrhage: 3.8% versus 2.8%, HR 1.38, over trial follow-up.

C23.label: insufficient
C23.reason: standing unopposed support is below the proof standard
C23.text: Absolute aspirin-related bleeding harm increases with age, particularly from age 60 onward, despite no apparent age difference in relative bleeding risk.

C24.label: accepted
C24.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C24.text: The USPSTF review found uncertainty about increased fatal gastrointestinal bleeding and no statistically significant increase in fatal hemorrhagic stroke.

C25.label: accepted
C25.reason: surviving support meets the proof standard
C25.text: The USPSTF concludes with moderate certainty that initiating low-dose aspirin for primary cardiovascular prevention in adults aged 60 or older has no net benefit and recommends against initiation. This is the body's benefit–harm assessment, not a measured finding of exactly zero effect or uniform net harm.
